title: non-blocking-fallback-allocator-and-slo-backpressure-bridge
author: Leah Ortega
release_notes: Introduce a non-blocking fallback allocator and SLO backpressure bridge to reduce tail-SLO violations during regional failover and KV cache thrash. Includes a hotfix for eviction thrashing and a gradual rollout plan.
description:
Motivation: During a recent partial-regional outage (SUP-9082) we observed head-of-line blocking when the primary fast-path exhausted capacity and requests were synchronously retried to fallback replicas. This caused transient but large tail latency spikes and KV cache thrash across regions. This PR adds a non-blocking fallback allocator combined with an SLO backpressure bridge to: 1) avoid synchronous blocking when requesting warm fallback slots, 2) soften routing so caller-facing requests see bounded latency even while fallback warming is in progress, and 3) prevent cascade eviction/rehydration cycles that amplify regional failover impact.

What this changes (high level): Implement a FallbackAllocator that returns immediately with a lightweight token when a preferred fast-path is saturated; the token encodes a soft priority and warm-up policy. A background warm-up worker takes tokens and provisions warm contexts (warming KV cache + small prefill steps) for fallback replicas. In parallel we add an SLOBackpressureBridge that coordinates request admission across tiers: it applies a gradual, tenant-weighted throttle (not drop) and routes a small fraction of requests to an isolated slowpath pool while the warm-up completes. The bridge also exposes signal hooks for Console (per-tenant SLO credit, active warming count) so operators can observe and adjust.

Key implementation details: - FallbackAllocator (runtime/allocator/fallback_allocator.go): new API allocateFallback(ctx, opts) -> (token, suggested_wait_ms). Fast-path code paths now call allocateFallback instead of blocking on sync acquire. - Warmup worker (runtime/allocator/warmup_worker.go): prioritized queue, exponential backoff on failures, max_concurrent_warmups per-region config. - SLOBackpressureBridge (gateway/backpressure/bridge.go): token acceptance, tenant-weighted admission, gradual ramping policy (ramp_up_ms config), and compatibility with existing circuit state. - KV eviction optimizer (runtime/cache/kv_eviction_heuristic.go): heuristic to avoid evicting recently-prefetched prefixes during a regional failover window; a short-lived sticky-keep policy reduces rehydrate churn. - Console metrics and tracing: new metrics rwi_fallback_tokens, rwi_warmups_in_progress, rwi_slo_bridge_throttle_pct; new trace spans warmup.prepare and bridge.admit.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/allocator/fallback_allocator.go (+tests) - runtime/allocator/warmup_worker.go (+integration test harness) - runtime/cache/kv_eviction_heuristic.go - gateway/backpressure/bridge.go - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (metrics added) - docs/operational/fallbacks.md (operator runbook + rollout steps) - scripts/e2e/regional_failover_smoke.sh (test harness)

Commits (summary): - 7 commits: initial allocator scaffolding; warmup worker + queue; backpressure bridge; KV eviction heuristic; metrics + traces; docs and tests; small followups & flake fixes.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover allocator token semantics and heuristic invariants. Integration harness simulates regional capacity loss and verifies: 1) tail latency P99 reduces by ~35% vs previous synchronous fallback under a synthetic spike, 2) warmup worker provisions fallback contexts within target ramp_up_ms in 95% of cases, 3) eviction churn drops (measured as rehydrates/sec) by ~60% during simulated failover windows. CI: initial run hit a flaky e2e test (race in warmup_worker) — fixed in follow-up commit. All checks pass on final run.

Rollout plan: staged rollout via release flags: - opt-in on Canary (10% of traffic) for 24h - widen to 30% for 48h if error rates and SLO credit burn look stable - full rollout after 7d if metrics hold. Console dashboards were added for quick rollback: warmup latency, fallback token rate, per-tenant throttle pct, rehydrate/sec.

Operator notes / runbook: docs/operational/fallbacks.md describes how to tune max_concurrent_warmups, ramp_up_ms, and sticky-keep window. Recommended defaults tuned for Dedicated and Hosted tiers are provided. If warmup worker falls behind, SLOBackpressureBridge automatically increases throttle_pct to protect global SLOs — operators can override via console.

Related: SUP-9082 (incident), ENG-4121 (epic: graceful-degradation), PM-892 (product requirement: bounded tail latency).

Why unique/different from previous approaches: existing fallbacks attempted synchronous context allocation (blocking; head-of-line risk) or immediate cold-routing (leading to cache churn). This hybrid approach intentionally returns lightweight tokens to callers and performs asynchronous warmup + soft admission, striking a balance between latency protection and cache stability.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids adding a global lock; coordination is local to region and tenant to reduce blast radius. All new public APIs are backward-compatible. Documentation includes migration steps for internal consumers and a short example for SDK teams to surface fallback token hints to caller logic.
